chapters.record: ADR-001 How should the design respect CON-001: Patient personal data must be handled in line with the health data regulation that applies where the clinic operates?
chapters.draft: This design choice addresses CON-001 by aligning the handling of patient personal data with applicable health data regulations where the clinic operates, ensuring the core constraint is respected. The decision considers the context of REQ-001, which enables patients to book appointments online at any time, incorporating the relevant quality drivers and constraints. The alternatives ALT-001 and ALT-002 illustrate the options between a single owned boundary or a separate independent boundary to manage regulated data effectively. The rationale prioritizes a clear ownership and boundary for compliance with health data regulations, informed by the constraint CON-001 and quality concerns in QD-001, supported by the project context in REQ-001. Operational and governance consequences, as well as obligations introduced by these choices, are identified in relevant patterns but are not yet decided here, leaving room for further verification and ownership assignment.

Enables patients to book appointments online at any time, fulfilling the requirement for round-the-clock appointment scheduling while excluding clinical records, prescriptions, and related booking or reminder functions handled elsewhere.

Owns Appointment scheduling: Patients can book an appointment at any time through the online service, covering online bookings only. Outside scope are clinical records and prescriptions, plus phone bookings and their management (register/move/cancel) and sending or handling appointment reminders by text or email, which are handled by other components.

When the provider fails or does not answer, the caller must handle the outcome as unavailable or uncertain. The specific behaviour upon such failure is currently open and requires decision based on usage context and operational conditions, consistent with the open question on failurePolicy in IF-001 and the lack of stated expectations in the upstream requirements and related components.

The control is a design proposal to limit access to the Appointment data, intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of confidential journey information. However, where and how this control is enforced remains an open question, as it is not stated in the brief or upstream records. The design must eventually define enforcement location and method, ownership, monitoring, failure handling, and review criteria to meet security obligations and address the high-priority threat of unauthorized disclosure.

chapters.record: SDD Sol live check · reference — Solution Design
chapters.draft: Sol live check · reference enables patients to book, move, or cancel outpatient appointments themselves at any time of day. The design also ensures that every freed slot is offered to the waiting list before the day of the appointment, supporting outpatient appointment management from booking through follow-up. Key unresolved decisions address how personal health data and appointment reminders conform to applicable regulations and performance requirements, while online booking must be operational by year-end.
